- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to adjust — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion to prevent overextension.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility penalty to forecast.
- When bullish sentiment is low but supply is negative, model often ignores bearish pressure — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% of recent mean or event-weighted volatility.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes followed by recovery, model may over-forecast recovery — apply smoothing or lagged decay to avoid premature rebound.
- In multi-event periods (e.g., 20+ events), model tends to overestimate stability — reduce forecast variance or apply event-weighted mean reversion.
